newsitem.title: USA: Sara Lee sees record sales, earnings.
newsitem.headline: Sara Lee sees record sales, earnings.

text.p: Sara Lee Corp said Thursday it expects to report record sales and earnings throughout the remainder of fiscal 1997.

Earlier, it reported net earnings for the second quarter ended December 28 of $0.64 a primary share, up 12.3 percent from $0.57 a year ago. Quarterly net sales gained 7.6 percent to $5.3 billion vs $4.9 billion.

"We are pleased to have posted increased sales in three of our four lines of business and higher operating profits for all four segments in our second quarter," John Bryan, chairman, said in a statement. "Of great importance to our company, tight working capital controls across all our businesses led to strong cash flow in the second quarter. These results reflected our continued focus on internal growth and improved returns as well as the benefits of select acquisitions completed in recent periods. We expect to report record sales and earnings throughout the remainder of the fiscal year."

Sara Lee said its packaged meats and bakery division sales rose 17.6 percent to $2.04 billion in the second quarter from $1.73 billion a year ago. Operating income in the quarter increased 12.1 percent to $149 million from $133 million.

The recent acquisition of French processed meats company Aoste helped results for this segment. Excluding acquisitions, unit volumes for worldwide packaged meats were flat for the quarter. Worldwide unit volumes for Sara Lee bakery fell five percent in the quarter.
Coffee and grocery division sales fell 6.4 percent to $731 million due to lower coffee prices and a stronger U.S. dollar.

Year-ago second quarter sales for coffee and grocery were $782.0 million. Operating income for this segment rose 6.6 percent in the quarter to $123.0 million from $115.0 million a year ago, reflecting lower coffee costs, improved operating efficiencies and increased sales of higher-margin products.

Sara Lee said its household and body care division had a 2.5 percent rise in second quarter sales to $440.0 million from $429 million. Quarterly operating income rose seven percent to $54.0 million from $50.0 million.
Personal products sales were up 5.6 percent in the second quarter to $2.07 billion from $1.96 billion. Operating income increased 5.1 percent to $236.0 million from $225 million.

Sales and profits for the quarter in this segment rose in the United States and Europe. By product category, global sales increased in the hosiery, knit products and intimate apparel areas. Profit growth was particularly strong for worldwide intimates.

Sara Lee said that, despite increased funding for acquisitions and share repurchase, net interest expense in the second quarter declined $2.0 million from a year ago to $44.0 million. This reflected the company's continued strong cash flow, it added.
